question: Should streaming services pay artists by the minutes people listen rather than by the number of plays?
answer: Per-play pay rewards cutting songs short and stuffing albums with brief tracks, since a 31-second play earns as much as a seven-minute one. Paying by time would stop punishing the long forms, from jazz to classical to ambient. Listeners give their minutes, not their clicks; the money should follow what they actually spend.
move: Whichever side you took, ask what each rule would tempt makers to produce.
ask: If I were paid for what I do, would the rule reward value or just volume?
counterpoint: Paying by the minute would reward padding instead. Spotify already had to rule, from 2024, that noise tracks must run at least two minutes to earn royalties, because rain and fan sounds left on all night were soaking up money. A three-minute song people choose again and again would lose to sound nobody is listening to.
reference: Spotify for Artists, Modernizing Our Royalty System to Drive an Additional $1 Billion toward Emerging and Professional Artists, November 2023
